title: A package-manager install into an empty project: thousands of changes, no quiescence, and the lockfile last

provenance.evidence: 327 readings carrying 12,225 changes over 5,662 distinct paths: 5,661 appearances, 6,545 in-place rewrites and 19 removals. The largest single reading held 108 changes. The install compiled a native module, so the run also contains a whole build tree. `package-lock.json` (73,837 bytes) and `node_modules/.package-lock.json` (74,010 bytes) both appear in the FINAL reading and in no earlier one.
provenance.excerpt_note: The stream below is an EXCERPT, renumbered densely, and it is the only pattern in this corpus that is not complete. It keeps the three facts a coalescer can be wrong about — the opening burst, the removal burst near the end, and the lockfile arriving last — and drops 12,000 middle events that are all the same shape. `observed_totals` carries what was dropped, and the command above re-captures the whole of it.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling
with 108 changes in one reading, anything created and removed inside a reading was certainly missed and its count is unknown

objects.role: an optional platform package removed near the end

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: At 108 changes per reading the backend's first declared restriction is doing most of the work: several writes to one file between two readings are one change, and the corpus cannot say how many were folded.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: The dependency tree and the lockfile that describes it, together. The lockfile is the only artefact of the install a person names, and it is written last, so a checkpoint that ends before it is a tree with no record of what produced it.
expected.forbidden_note: Every point before the lockfile is a half-installed tree. They are all real states and none is a save. This is the pattern that shows the difference between the two: a coalescer that never emits a state that did not exist can still emit thousands of states nobody wanted.

notes: 12,225 changes with no quiescence is what makes the maximum-uncheckpointed-bytes and maximum-uncheckpointed-time triggers unavoidable: a rule that only emits at quiescence keeps the whole install uncheckpointed, and plan §3.5 ACT-004 requires stable work to survive a daemon failure.

Every split those triggers force lands on a forbidden sequence point, by construction, because every point except the last one is forbidden. The corpus therefore does NOT assert one checkpoint here under a byte trigger; it asserts one checkpoint under quiescence and records that a byte-triggered split is honest but not meaningful.
This is the pattern the idle-interval and byte-budget defaults must be chosen against, and this run does not choose them. See ../README.md section 7.
